name: Microscope
desc: The frame goes under the objective — a lit field stop with the lamp's hot spot wandering across it, a cell culture crawling past as the stage is scanned, debris adrift in another focal plane and a reticle ticking off the millimetres, offered as brightfield, darkfield, phase halo, crossed-polar interference colour or a fluorescence tag that slowly photobleaches.

energy.doc: lamp gain — how hard the field is lit and how much the pass emits

scale.doc: field-stop diameter: 0.35 is a tight peephole, 2.4 throws the stop off-frame entirely

density.doc: how confluent the culture is — fraction of cells actually present

mag.doc: magnification — 0 is a wide low-power field of many small cells, 1 is a few big ones

focus.doc: focus: 0 throws the specimen and the debris right out, 1 is a crisp cut

hue.doc: lamp colour temperature (44 = tungsten); the specimen and reticle take complements off it

speed.doc: stage-scan and debris rate (the bench-vibration floor is deliberately independent of this)

x.doc: optical axis x — where the eyepiece field sits

alpha.doc: master opacity of the whole pass

style.doc: which contrast technique is on the scope — these differ in what makes the image, not just in hue: absorption, scattered light, phase halo, interference colour, or emission

act.doc: multi-minute program: a steady stage scan, hunting focus back and forth, or stepping up magnification section by section
